questions.q: Reference table — LASER WAVELENGTHS. Which laser/wavelength pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.exp:
Ruby laser is 694 nm, NOT 532 nm. Correct table: KTP 532, PDL 585/595, Ruby 694, Alexandrite 755, Diode 810, Nd:YAG 1064, Er:YAG 2940, CO2 10600 nm.
🏰 Palace: RUBY GEM glows DEEP RED at 694 nm — anyone claiming a 532 nm ruby is a castle IMPOSTER (532 is the GREEN KTP twins).

questions.q: Reference table — CHROMOPHORE PEAKS. Oxyhaemoglobin has absorption peaks best matched by which laser group?
questions.exp:
Oxyhaemoglobin peaks: 418 (Soret), 542, 577 nm. Vascular lasers KTP 532 and PDL 585/595 sit on these peaks. CO2/Er:YAG target water; ruby/alexandrite target melanin.
🏰 Palace: BLOOD VESSELS love GREEN (532) and YELLOW (595) light — the PDL VAMPIRE and KTP SNIPER feast on oxyhaemoglobin peaks.

questions.q: Reference table — TCA FROSTING LEVELS. Level II frosting corresponds to which histological depth?
opts: White frosting with erythema showing through — papillary dermis
Solid dense white-grey — upper reticular dermis
Speckled white on erythema — epidermis only
questions.exp:
Frosting: Level I = speckled white on pink (epidermis); Level II = white with erythema showing through (papillary dermis); Level III = solid white-grey, no erythema (upper reticular dermis). CROSS targets Level II–III within scars.
🏰 Palace: FROST LEVELS climb the castle: L1 SPECKLED PINK (top), L2 WHITE-WITH-PINK-BLEED (papillary), L3 SOLID GREY ICE (reticular).

questions.q: Reference table — FITZPATRICK SKIN TYPES. Type IV is characterised by:
opts: Always tans, rarely burns — light brown/Mediterranean skin
Never burns, deeply pigmented — black skin
Always burns, never tans — pale white
Burns minimally, tans well — darker white
questions.exp:
Fitzpatrick: I always burns/never tans; II usually burns/tans minimally; III sometimes burns/tans uniformly; IV rarely burns/tans easily (Mediterranean); V very rarely burns (brown); VI never burns (black).
🏰 Palace: TYPE IV is the MEDITERRANEAN KNIGHT — RARELY BURNS, ALWAYS TANS olive-brown under the castle sun.

questions.q: Reference table — PEEL DEPTHS. Which agent is classified as a MEDIUM-depth peel?
questions.exp:
Superficial: glycolic 20–70% (brief), SA 20–30%, Jessner's, TCA 10–30%. Medium: TCA 35–50%, Jessner+TCA 35%, glycolic 70%+TCA 35%. Deep: phenol-croton oil (Baker-Gordon).
🏰 Palace: MEDIUM PEEL = TCA 35–50% in the middle floor of the peel castle — superficial below (glycolic/SA), deep PHENOL dungeon above no — below.

questions.q: Reference table — BOTOX DOSING (onabotulinumtoxinA). Standard total dose for the glabellar complex is:
questions.exp:
FDA-approved glabellar dose: 20U = 4U at each of 5 points (procerus ×1, corrugators ×4). Crow's feet 12U/side, forehead 10–20U, masseter 20–30U/side.
🏰 Palace: GLABELLA = 4×5 = 20 UNITS, the FIVE-POINT FROWN STAR each loaded with 4 toxin arrows.

questions.q: Reference table — FILLER G-PRIME (G'). A HIGH G' (high elastic modulus) filler is best suited for:
opts: Skin bioremodelling in the superficial dermis
Fine superficial lines — tear trough, lips
Deep structural support — chin, cheekbone, jawline projection
questions.exp:
High G' (firm, high lift) fillers resist deformation → deep supraperiosteal structural augmentation (chin, malar, jaw). Low G' (soft) fillers → fine lines, lips, tear trough. G' = elastic/storage modulus.
🏰 Palace: HIGH G-PRIME = STIFF STONE BLOCKS for building castle PILLARS (chin, cheekbone); LOW G-PRIME = SOFT CLAY for delicate LIP carving.

questions.q: Reference table — 5-ALPHA REDUCTASE. Finasteride selectively inhibits which isoenzyme, and where is it predominant?
opts: Type 2 — predominant in hair follicle dermal papilla, prostate, genital skin
Type 1 — predominant in sebaceous glands and skin
questions.exp:
5-AR Type 1: sebaceous glands, non-genital skin, scalp. Type 2: hair follicle dermal papilla, prostate, genital skin, liver. Finasteride blocks Type 2; dutasteride blocks both 1 and 2.
🏰 Palace: FINASTERIDE targets TYPE 2 (the HAIR FOLLICLE + PROSTATE guard); DUTASTERIDE is the DOUBLE agent hitting BOTH types.

questions.q: Reference table — SUNSCREEN FILTERS. Which is a PHYSICAL (inorganic) UV filter?
questions.exp:
Physical/inorganic filters: zinc oxide (broad UVA+UVB), titanium dioxide (UVB+UVA2). Chemical/organic: avobenzone (UVA1), oxybenzone, octocrylene, octinoxate, homosalate.
🏰 Palace: ZINC OXIDE is the MINERAL SHIELD WALL (physical) reflecting sun; AVOBENZONE & friends are CHEMICAL SPONGES that absorb.

questions.q: Reference table — HAIR CYCLE. The approximate duration of the ANAGEN phase of scalp hair is:
questions.exp:
Anagen (growth) 2–6 years (determines hair length); catagen (regression) 2–3 weeks; telogen (rest) 2–3 months. ~85–90% of scalp hairs in anagen at any time.
🏰 Palace: ANAGEN is the LONG REIGN — 2–6 YEARS on the throne; CATAGEN a 2–3 WEEK abdication; TELOGEN a 2–3 MONTH retirement.

questions.q: Reference table — MELANIN-TARGETING LASERS for hair removal by skin type. Which is SAFEST for Fitzpatrick VI?
questions.exp:
Lower melanin absorption + deeper penetration = safer in dark skin. Nd:YAG 1064 nm is the gold standard for types V–VI. Alexandrite/ruby/diode have higher epidermal melanin absorption (risk of burns/PIH in dark skin).
🏰 Palace: ND:YAG 1064 = the DARK-SKIN-SAFE DEEP DIVER, ignoring epidermal melanin walls; ALEXANDRITE/RUBY are too MELANIN-GREEDY for type VI.

questions.q: Reference table — VITAMIN C. L-ascorbic acid requires which formulation pH for skin penetration?
questions.exp:
L-ascorbic acid (pKa 4.2) penetrates only at pH <3.5 (uncharged form). Minimum 10% concentration; plateaus at 20%. Higher pH → ionised → no penetration. Derivatives (MAP, ascorbyl glucoside) work at higher pH.
🏰 Palace: VITAMIN C the ACID DIVA performs only in the pH <3.5 ACIDIC ARENA — raise the pH and she ionises, locked out of the skin gate.

questions.q: Reference table — THERMAL RELAXATION TIME (TRT). The TRT of a typical terminal hair follicle (~200–300 µm) is approximately:
questions.exp:
TRT ∝ diameter². Melanosome (~1µm) ≈ 1µs; tattoo ink (~0.1µm) ≈ ns–ps; hair follicle (~200–300µm) ≈ 40–100 ms; leg vein (~1mm) ≈ seconds. Pulse duration ≤ TRT for selectivity.
🏰 Palace: HAIR FOLLICLE TRT = 40–100 ms milliseconds (medium target); TINY MELANOSOMES cool in MICROSECONDS, BIG VEINS take SECONDS.

questions.q: Reference table — PHENOL-CROTON OIL PEEL. The agent in the Baker-Gordon formula responsible for the DEPTH of penetration (epidermolysis intensity) is:
questions.exp:
Modern Hetter/Stone studies showed CROTON OIL concentration — not phenol % — is the key determinant of peel depth. Higher croton oil = deeper peel. Phenol alone is keratocoagulant; croton oil is the vesicant driving depth.
🏰 Palace: CROTON OIL is the SECRET DEPTH CHARGE in the phenol peel — more croton drops = DEEPER DETONATION; phenol just sets the stage.

questions.q: Reference table — IPL CUT-OFF FILTERS. A 560 nm cut-off filter on an IPL device transmits wavelengths:
opts: Exactly 560 nm monochromatic — like a laser
400–560 nm band only — for superficial pigment
≥560 nm (blocks shorter wavelengths) — used for pigment and vascular lesions
≤560 nm only — used for deep hair removal
questions.exp:
IPL cut-off filters block wavelengths SHORTER than the stated number, transmitting longer ones. A 560nm filter passes 560–1200nm. Higher cut-offs (640, 695nm) spare more epidermal melanin → safer in darker skin/hair removal.
🏰 Palace: 560 CUT-OFF = a CASTLE GATE that only lets in LONG-WAVELENGTH guests (≥560), turning away the short blue-UV crowd.

questions.q: Reference table — LUDWIG vs NORWOOD-HAMILTON. The Norwood-Hamilton scale classifies:
questions.exp:
Norwood-Hamilton: male AGA, 7 stages (bitemporal recession → vertex → confluent). Ludwig: female AGA, 3 grades (crown thinning, frontal line preserved). Sinclair: 5-stage female scale. SALT: alopecia areata.
🏰 Palace: NORWOOD = MALE 7-STAGE BALD MAP (receding crown kingdom); LUDWIG = FEMALE 3-GRADE crown thinning.

questions.q: Reference table — INJECTABLE FILLER REVERSAL. Which filler is REVERSIBLE with hyaluronidase?
questions.exp:
Only HA fillers are dissolvable with hyaluronidase. CaHA, PLLA, and PMMA are NOT reversible enzymatically. This is why HA is preferred in high-risk vascular zones (nose, glabella).
🏰 Palace: ONLY HA melts under the HYALURONIDASE FIRE KEY; CaHA/PLLA/PMMA are PERMANENT STONE with no enzymatic unlock.

questions.q: Reference table — MINOXIDIL. Minoxidil is a prodrug activated in the scalp by which enzyme?
opts: Sulfotransferase (SULT1A1) — converts minoxidil to minoxidil sulfate
questions.exp:
Minoxidil is activated to minoxidil sulfate by follicular sulfotransferase SULT1A1. Low SULT1A1 activity (~30–40% of people) explains topical minoxidil non-response. It opens K+ channels → vasodilation + anagen prolongation.
🏰 Palace: SULT1A1 is the SCALP GATE-KEEPER stamping MINOXIDIL'S passport (to sulfate) — ~35% lack the stamp = NON-RESPONDERS.

questions.q: Reference table — BOTULINUM SEROTYPES & TARGETS. BoNT type B (rimabotulinumtoxinB) cleaves which SNARE protein?
questions.exp:
SNARE cleavage: A & E → SNAP-25; B, D, F, G → VAMP/synaptobrevin; C → syntaxin + SNAP-25. Type A (Botox) and Type B (Myobloc) are the clinically used serotypes.
🏰 Palace: BoNT-B cuts the VAMP rope (synaptobrevin); BoNT-A cuts SNAP-25 — different scissors for different SNARE cables.

questions.q: Reference table — HYPERHIDROSIS BOTOX. The standard botulinum toxin A dose per axilla for axillary hyperhidrosis is:
questions.exp:
Axillary hyperhidrosis: 50U onabotulinumtoxinA per axilla (100U total), injected as 10–15 intradermal points mapped by Minor's starch-iodine test. Palms need higher doses (~100U/palm) but risk hand weakness.
🏰 Palace: AXILLA = 50 UNITS each pit (100 total) sprinkled in a GRID over the sweaty starch-iodine map.

questions.q: Reference table — WOOD'S LAMP FLUORESCENCE. Which condition fluoresces CORAL-RED?
questions.exp:
Coral-red = erythrasma (porphyrins). Blue-green = Microsporum tinea capitis + Pseudomonas. Pale yellow = tinea versicolor. Bright blue-white enhancement = vitiligo/depigmentation. Ash-leaf macules = blue-white.
🏰 Palace: CORAL REEF RED glow = ERYTHRASMA (Corynebacterium porphyrin party); GREEN glow = MICROSPORUM/Pseudomonas.

questions.q: Reference table — PDL SETTINGS. The classic pulsed dye laser wavelength(s) for vascular lesions is/are:
questions.exp:
PDL operates at 585nm (original) or 595nm (longer, deeper penetration for larger vessels). Both sit near the oxyhaemoglobin 577nm peak. Used for port-wine stains, telangiectasia, haemangioma, rosacea, warts, scars.
🏰 Palace: PDL = 585/595 nm YELLOW VAMPIRE light feasting on oxyhaemoglobin at the 577 peak.

questions.q: Reference table — KELOID FIRST-LINE. The first-line treatment for most keloids is:
questions.exp:
Intralesional triamcinolone (ILT, 10–40mg/mL q4–6wk) is first-line — inhibits fibroblasts, reduces collagen. Often combined with 5-FU or cryotherapy. Surgery ALONE has 45–100% recurrence; must combine with adjuvant (ILT/radiation/pressure).
🏰 Palace: KELOID first move = TRIAMCINOLONE FLOOD (10–40 mg/mL) to crumble the overbuilt scar wall — NEVER cut alone (recurrence dragon).

questions.q: Reference table — GLOGAU PHOTOAGING. Glogau Type II is characterised by:
opts: Early wrinkles, 'wrinkles in motion', age 30s–40s, early actinic keratoses
Severe wrinkling, only wrinkles, yellow-grey skin, 60s+
questions.exp:
Glogau: I = no wrinkles (mild, 20–30s); II = wrinkles in motion (moderate, 30–40s, early AKs); III = wrinkles at rest (advanced, 50s, telangiectasia, dyschromia); IV = only wrinkles (severe, 60–70s, yellow-grey, prior skin cancers).
🏰 Palace: GLOGAU II = 'WRINKLES IN MOTION' — lines show only when the 30–40s face MOVES; by III they're carved at REST.

questions.q: Reference table — CRYOLIPOLYSIS. Adipocyte apoptosis during cryolipolysis occurs at a target temperature of approximately:
questions.exp:
Cryolipolysis cools fat to ~−11°C: triglycerides crystallise at higher temperatures than water, so adipocytes undergo apoptosis while overlying skin/water-rich tissue is spared. Fat cleared by macrophages over 4–12 weeks (~20–25% reduction).
🏰 Palace: −11°C is the FAT-FREEZE SWEET SPOT — OLIVE-OIL adipocytes crystallise while the WATERY skin walls stay liquid and safe.

questions.q: Reference table — HA FILLER VASCULAR EMERGENCY. The immediate hyaluronidase dose for impending skin necrosis from vascular occlusion is:
opts: Do not use hyaluronidase; warm compress only
High dose 300–1500 IU into the affected zone immediately
questions.exp:
Vascular occlusion = emergency. Inject hyaluronidase 300–1500 IU immediately into/around the ischaemic area, repeat hourly. Adjuncts: warmth, massage, topical GTN, aspirin. Ocular involvement → urgent ophthalmology + retrobulbar hyaluronidase.
🏰 Palace: OCCLUSION FIRE = 300–1500 IU HYALURONIDASE HOSE blasted IMMEDIATELY — every minute of delay spreads the NECROSIS BLAZE.

questions.q: Reference table — SPF MATH. An SPF 30 sunscreen blocks approximately what percentage of UVB?
questions.exp:
SPF blocks: SPF15 ≈ 93%, SPF30 ≈ 97%, SPF50 ≈ 98%. Diminishing returns above SPF50. SPF measures UVB protection (erythema); UVA protection shown by PA+ system or broad-spectrum label.
🏰 Palace: SPF 30 = 97% UVB BLOCKED; SPF 15 = 93%, SPF 50 = 98% — after 30 it's DIMINISHING castle-wall returns.

questions.q: Reference table — TRETINOIN POTENCY. Rank topical retinoids from LEAST to MOST irritating/potent (per equivalent %):
questions.exp:
Conversion chain (least→most active): retinyl ester → retinol → retinaldehyde → retinoic acid (tretinoin, the receptor-active form). Each step = an oxidation. Retinol ~20× weaker than tretinoin but better tolerated.
🏰 Palace: RETINOID LADDER: ESTER (basement) → RETINOL → RETINAL → TRETINOIN (throne) — each rung climbs in POTENCY and IRRITATION.

questions.q: Reference table — NAIL/CUTICLE ANATOMY. The eponychium refers to:
opts: The thickened skin under the free edge
The white half-moon at the nail base
The proximal nail fold's thin epidermal cuticle covering the nail base
questions.exp:
Eponychium = cuticle, the proximal nail fold's keratin seal over the nail plate. Lunula = white half-moon (visible distal matrix). Hyponychium = under the free edge. Paronychium = lateral folds.
🏰 Palace: EPONYCHIUM = the CUTICLE CASTLE-GATE SEAL at the nail base; LUNULA = the WHITE MOON window; HYPONYCHIUM = the under-edge dungeon.

questions.q: Reference table — ABO/ER:YAG ABLATION. Compared to CO2, the Er:YAG (2940 nm) water absorption coefficient is approximately:
opts: ~10–16× higher → more precise ablation, less thermal coagulation
questions.exp:
Er:YAG 2940nm sits at the water absorption peak (~16× higher than CO2 10600nm). Result: precise micro-ablation (5–20µm/pass), minimal residual thermal damage (less coagulation/haemostasis), faster healing, but less collagen tightening than CO2.
🏰 Palace: ER:YAG is 16× THIRSTIER for water than CO2 — it ablates with SURGICAL PRECISION and minimal CHAR, but less COLLAGEN-SHRINK heat.

questions.q: Reference table — DEPIGMENTING MECHANISMS. Hydroquinone reduces melanin by:
opts: Inhibiting tyrosinase (competing with tyrosine) + melanocyte cytotoxicity
Chelating copper at tyrosinase active site (kojic-like)
questions.exp:
Hydroquinone competitively inhibits tyrosinase and is cytotoxic to melanocytes (inhibits DNA/RNA synthesis). Kojic acid = copper chelation; niacinamide = blocks melanosome transfer; arbutin = HQ derivative; azelaic acid = tyrosinase inhibition + cytotoxic to abnormal melanocytes.
🏰 Palace: HYDROQUINONE both JAMS tyrosinase AND POISONS the melanocyte factory; KOJIC steals copper; NIACINAMIDE blocks the delivery van.

questions.q: Reference table — AZELAIC ACID. Azelaic acid's dual cosmetic indications are:
questions.exp:
Azelaic acid (15–20%): antibacterial against C. acnes, anti-comedonal, anti-inflammatory (acne/rosacea papulopustular), AND tyrosinase inhibition + selective cytotoxicity to hyperactive melanocytes (melasma, PIH). Safe in pregnancy.
🏰 Palace: AZELAIC ACID is the DOUBLE-DUTY KNIGHT — fights ACNE bacteria AND bleaches MELASMA by jamming tyrosinase, safe even for pregnant queens.

questions.q: Reference table — MICRONEEDLING DEPTHS. The recommended needle depth for ATROPHIC ACNE SCARS on the cheek is:
questions.exp:
Microneedling depth by indication: 0.25–0.5mm periorbital/fine lines; 0.5–1.0mm general rejuvenation/pigment; 1.5–2.5mm acne scars/stretch marks (cheek thickness allows deeper). Deeper than skin thickness risks bruising/PIH.
🏰 Palace: ACNE SCARS on the CHEEK = DEEP 1.5–2.5mm needles; delicate EYE area = SHORT 0.25–0.5mm arrows.

questions.q: Reference table — THREAD MATERIALS. Among absorbable lifting threads, rank longevity (shortest → longest):
questions.exp:
Absorption/effect duration: PDO (polydioxanone) ~6mo absorb, 12–18mo effect; PLLA (poly-L-lactic) ~12–18mo, longer collagen effect; PCL (polycaprolactone) ~18–24mo, longest. Longer absorption = longer neocollagenesis.
🏰 Palace: THREAD LIFESPAN ladder: PDO (shortest) → PLLA → PCL (longest) — the SLOWER it dissolves, the LONGER the collagen castle stands.

questions.q: Reference table — SCLEROSANTS. The recommended sclerosant for small reticular/spider leg veins (1–3 mm) is:
questions.exp:
Concentration scales with vein size. Spider/reticular (1–3mm): polidocanol 0.25–1% or STS 0.1–0.3%. Larger varicose veins need higher concentrations or foam. Too-high concentration in tiny veins → telangiectatic matting + PSH.
🏰 Palace: SMALL SPIDER VEINS need WEAK 0.5–1% polidocanol — overdose the tiny vessels and you breed MATTING + RUST STAINS.

questions.q: Reference table — ALEXANDRITE INDICATION. Alexandrite 755 nm is the gold-standard hair-removal laser for which skin types?
questions.exp:
Alexandrite 755nm has high melanin absorption → excellent for light skin/dark hair (types I–III). Too risky for V–VI (epidermal melanin competition → burns/PIH); use Nd:YAG 1064 for dark skin. Diode 810 spans III–IV.
🏰 Palace: ALEXANDRITE 755 = the LIGHT-SKIN/DARK-HAIR specialist (I–III); hand DARK skin to the ND:YAG deep diver.

questions.q: Reference table — BOTOX ONSET & DURATION. Typical onset and duration of cosmetic botulinum toxin A effect:
opts: Onset 2–7 days, peak ~2 weeks, duration 3–4 months
questions.exp:
BoNT-A: onset 2–7 days, peak effect ~10–14 days, duration 3–4 months (cosmetic). Duration extends with repeated use (muscle atrophy). Reconstituted toxin should be used within 24h (some data up to 4 weeks refrigerated).
🏰 Palace: BOTOX wakes in 2–7 DAYS, PEAKS at 2 WEEKS, reigns 3–4 MONTHS before the wrinkles return.

questions.q: Reference table — PIGMENT DISORDERS DEPTH. The Wood's lamp ENHANCES (sharpens border of) which type of melasma?
opts: Mixed melasma at the dermal component
questions.exp:
Wood's lamp: epidermal melasma is ENHANCED (margins sharpen, contrast increases — pigment is superficial). Dermal melasma shows NO enhancement (deeper pigment). Mixed = some areas enhance. This guides prognosis: epidermal responds best to topicals.
🏰 Palace: WOOD'S LAMP SHARPENS EPIDERMAL melasma (surface pigment lights up the border); DERMAL melasma stays BLURRY (pigment hides deep).

questions.q: Reference table — COLLAGEN TYPES. The predominant collagen type in normal adult DERMIS is:
questions.exp:
Adult dermis: ~80–85% type I, ~15% type III. Fetal/early-wound/scar dermis is type III-rich (reverses with maturation). Type IV = basement membrane; Type VII = anchoring fibrils (target in EB/lichen planus pemphigoides).
🏰 Palace: ADULT DERMIS = TYPE I COLLAGEN castle (80%+); BABY/SCAR skin is TYPE III-heavy; TYPE IV is the BASEMENT membrane floor.

questions.q: Reference table — RF MICRONEEDLING. The advantage of INSULATED vs non-insulated RF microneedles is:
opts: Insulated needles penetrate deeper than non-insulated
Insulated needles deliver RF only at the tip, sparing the epidermis → safer in dark skin
Insulation increases epidermal heating for better resurfacing
questions.exp:
Insulated RF microneedles have a non-conductive coating along the shaft, releasing energy only at the exposed tip in the deep dermis — epidermis is protected → lower PIH risk in darker skin. Non-insulated deliver energy along the full needle (more epidermal effect).
🏰 Palace: INSULATED NEEDLES = LIGHTNING RODS firing ONLY at the deep TIP, the EPIDERMIS roof stays cool and safe (great for dark skin).

questions.q: Reference table — ACNE SCAR SUBTYPES. The acne scar type LEAST responsive to resurfacing and best treated with TCA CROSS/punch techniques is:
questions.exp:
Ice-pick scars (narrow, deep, V-shaped) extend deep into dermis → poorly responsive to surface resurfacing; best treated with TCA CROSS or punch excision/elevation. Rolling → subcision. Boxcar → fractional laser/punch. Hypertrophic → steroids/5-FU.
🏰 Palace: ICE-PICK SCARS are deep NARROW WELLS — resurfacing skims the top uselessly; you need TCA CROSS down the chimney or a PUNCH to evict them.

questions.q: Reference table — PHOTODYNAMIC THERAPY. The photosensitiser converted to protoporphyrin IX in PDT is:
questions.exp:
ALA/MAL is taken up by abnormal cells and metabolised via the haem pathway to protoporphyrin IX (PpIX), which accumulates and is photoactivated (blue 417nm or red 630nm) generating singlet oxygen. Used for actinic keratoses, superficial BCC, acne, field cancerisation.
🏰 Palace: ALA/MAL CREAM becomes PpIX (the glowing photosensitiser bomb) inside abnormal cells — RED or BLUE light detonates it into singlet-oxygen shrapnel.

questions.q: Reference table — TXA FOR MELASMA. The mechanism of oral tranexamic acid in melasma is:
opts: Inhibits plasminogen→plasmin, reducing UV-induced prostaglandins/arachidonic acid that stimulate melanocytes
questions.exp:
Tranexamic acid (antifibrinolytic) blocks plasminogen activation on keratinocytes/melanocytes, reducing arachidonic acid and prostaglandins (and α-MSH), thereby decreasing UV-driven melanocyte activation and neovascularisation. Dose 250mg BD; caution re: thrombosis.
🏰 Palace: TXA cuts the PLASMIN SUPPLY LINE that feeds the UV→prostaglandin→melanocyte SIGNAL CHAIN — starving melasma at its trigger.

questions.q: Reference table — LIP DANGER. The highest-risk vessel for occlusion during lip/perioral filler is:
opts: Angular artery at the nasal tip
Superior/inferior labial arteries (branches of the facial artery)
questions.exp:
Lip filler vascular risk: superior and inferior labial arteries (facial artery branches) run in the wet-dry border/submucosal plane ~at the vermilion. Inject superficially in the body, avoid deep submucosal boluses. (Glabella/nose risk = supratrochlear/dorsal nasal → blindness.)
🏰 Palace: LIP DANGER = LABIAL ARTERIES hiding at the wet-dry border; inject too deep and you spear the facial-artery branch.

questions.q: Reference table — SALICYLIC ACID. Salicylic acid is classified as which type of agent and is especially useful for:
opts: Alpha-hydroxy acid — hydrophilic, for dry skin
Beta-hydroxy acid (BHA) — lipophilic, penetrates sebum → comedonal/oily acne
questions.exp:
Salicylic acid is a lipophilic beta-hydroxy acid (BHA) that penetrates sebaceous follicles → keratolytic and comedolytic, ideal for oily/comedonal acne. AHAs (glycolic, lactic) are hydrophilic, working on the surface for dryness/photoaging. SA also anti-inflammatory.
🏰 Palace: SALICYLIC ACID the OILY-LOVING BHA dives into SEBUM-FILLED PORES (lipophilic) to unplug comedones; AHAs stay on the WATERY surface.

questions.q: Reference table — ND:YAG TATTOO. For BLACK tattoo ink, the best Q-switched wavelength is:
questions.exp:
Tattoo ink targeting: black/dark blue → 1064nm (deepest, carbon-absorbing); red → 532nm; green → 694 ruby/755 alexandrite; yellow/orange → 532nm (most resistant). Picosecond pulses improve clearance of resistant colours.
🏰 Palace: BLACK INK = 1064 nm DARK HUNTER; RED INK = 532 green light; GREEN INK = 694/755 — match the laser to the ink colour wheel.

questions.q: Reference table — HEDGEHOG/BCC AESTHETIC OVERLAP. Curettage-and-electrodessication endpoint for superficial BCC is:
opts: Frost to Level III with TCA
Repeat curettage until firm normal dermis is felt (3 cycles typical)
questions.exp:
C&E for low-risk superficial BCC: curette the friable tumour (softer than dermis) then electrodessicate; repeat ×3 cycles until only firm normal dermis remains. ~5-year cure ~90% for well-selected lesions. Not for high-risk sites/aggressive subtypes.
🏰 Palace: C&E = SCRAPE the SOFT TUMOUR MUSH, ZAP, repeat ×3 until you feel FIRM NORMAL DERMIS bedrock under the curette.

questions.q: Reference table — POROKERATOSIS/UV INDEX. The UV index threshold above which sun protection is universally recommended is:
questions.exp:
UV Index: 1–2 low, 3–5 moderate, 6–7 high, 8–10 very high, 11+ extreme. Protection (broad-spectrum SPF30+, shade, clothing) is recommended at UVI ≥3. Cosmetic photoprotection counselling uses this scale.
🏰 Palace: UV INDEX 3 = the SUN-PROTECTION ALARM line; below 3 relax, at 3+ raise the SUNSCREEN SHIELD.

questions.q: Reference table — HORI'S vs OTA vs MELASMA. Acquired bilateral naevus of Ota-like macules (Hori's naevus) differ from melasma in that the pigment is:
opts: Dermal (blue-grey dermal melanocytes) — responds to Q-switched lasers, not topicals
questions.exp:
Hori's naevus (ABNOM): bilateral blue-grey-brown macules over malar area from DERMAL melanocytes → responds to Q-switched 1064/694 lasers (like naevus of Ota), NOT to topical bleaching. Melasma is epidermal/mixed and hormone/UV-driven, treated with topicals/TXA.
🏰 Palace: HORI'S = DERMAL blue-grey melanocytes needing Q-SWITCHED LASER; MELASMA = surface pigment for HYDROQUINONE — don't confuse the two malar masqueraders.

questions.q: Reference table — FRACTIONAL PHOTOTHERMOLYSIS. In fractional lasers, each microthermal/treatment zone (MTZ) is surrounded by spared tissue, which:
opts: Eliminates any need for collagen remodelling
Acts as a reservoir of viable cells enabling rapid re-epithelialisation and lower downtime than fully ablative
Prevents all thermal effect on the dermis
Increases scarring risk compared to fully ablative resurfacing
questions.exp:
Fractional lasers create columns of injury (MTZs) separated by untreated skin.
